r1.question: what should be done about a big group booked in this cafe?
r1.prediction: for a booked group, turning the music down 5 dB and the air 1 C cooler from 20 minutes before they arrive keeps the group and the other guests longer

experiment.method: before-after on the cafe's own record
experiment.setup: four Friday afternoons with a booked group of 10+ vs four without
experiment.procedure: compared mean stay of all guests 15:00-17:00, music -5 dB and air -1 C applied from 14:40
experiment.success_criteria: stay at least 10% longer with the adjustment, t-test p < 0.05
experiment.limitations: four days each side; one group had a birthday cake, which may have held them

r2.question: what do people want from this room when it rains?
r2.prediction: when the 2-hour forecast turns to rain, guests stay longer if the room is a touch warmer (+0.5 C) and brighter (+50 lux); cooling further makes them leave

experiment.setup: six rainy afternoons, alternating the adjustment on and off
experiment.procedure: from the first rain forecast, +0.5 C and +50 lux on 'on' days; baseline on 'off' days
experiment.success_criteria: stay longer on 'on' days, t-test p < 0.05
experiment.results: stay 29 vs 24 min, p = 0.04; entered unchanged
experiment.limitations: six days; heavy-rain days only twice

r3.question: what works in this room on a very hot day?
r3.prediction: on days over 33 C outside, one notch more fan and 0.5 C cooler keeps people longer

experiment.limitations: two days is too few; retest when more hot days are recorded

r4.question: what should be done when the cafe closes early?
r4.prediction: dimming by 150 lux and turning the music down 4 dB from 45 minutes before last order lets guests finish naturally; nobody has to be asked to leave and the last hour's stay is unchanged

experiment.setup: five early-close evenings with the wind-down vs four without
experiment.procedure: -150 lux and -4 dB from 45 minutes before last order
experiment.metrics: guests still seated at close, mean stay of the last hour
experiment.success_criteria: fewer than 3 guests seated at close, last-hour stay not shorter
experiment.results: 1.4 vs 5.5 seated at close; stay 22 vs 23 min
experiment.limitations: early closes are rare; five evenings

r5.question: what should be done when there is an event in this cafe?
r5.prediction: turning the music up 4 dB and the lights down 100 lux during a live set was tested and made guests leave faster; during an event leave volume and light at the baseline and only add one notch of fan for the crowd

experiment.setup: four live-music evenings with +4 dB / -100 lux vs four at baseline
experiment.procedure: settings switched from the set's start
experiment.metrics: departures per occupant-minute during the set, mean stay
experiment.results: departures 0.021 vs 0.014 per occupant-minute, worse; stay 24 vs 30 min
experiment.limitations: different acts each night; the crowd noise itself may have driven departures

r6.question: what should be done during maintenance or a delivery in this cafe?
r6.prediction: one notch more fan during a delivery hour (door open, CO2 and dust up) with lights unchanged; the effect on stay is unclear

experiment.setup: three delivery mornings with fan +1 vs three without
experiment.metrics: CO2 peak, mean stay in that hour
experiment.success_criteria: CO2 peak lower and stay unchanged
experiment.results: CO2 peak 740 vs 810 ppm; stay 19 vs 21 min, not significant
experiment.limitations: three mornings; deliveries vary in length

r7.question: what should be done when children or students fill this cafe?
r7.prediction: on school-holiday afternoons, 100 lux brighter and 0.5 C cooler lengthens stays; the room is noisier anyway, so the music can come down 3 dB without anyone noticing

experiment.procedure: +100 lux, -0.5 C, -3 dB from 14:00 on 'on' days

r8.question: what settings suit this room on a quiet day?
r8.prediction: dimming below 350 lux on a quiet afternoon shortens the stays of the few guests who are there; on a quiet day keep the light at the baseline and save energy on the fan instead

experiment.setup: eight afternoons under 8 seated, alternating -200 lux and baseline
experiment.results: stay 18 vs 24 min, dim days worse, p = 0.02
experiment.limitations: quiet afternoons cluster in the same month

r9.question: what should be done on a promotion day in this cafe?
r9.prediction: on a promotion day the room fills faster than the fan clears CO2; fan +1 from open keeps CO2 under the 1000 ppm limit and stays are unchanged

experiment.setup: three promotion days with fan +1 from open vs two without
experiment.metrics: minutes over 1000 ppm CO2, mean stay
experiment.success_criteria: no minute over 1000 ppm, stay unchanged
experiment.results: 0 vs 76 minutes over the limit; stay 25 vs 24 min
experiment.limitations: five days; promotions differ in pull

r10.question: what settings suit a Friday in this cafe?
r10.prediction: Fridays run warmer and louder after 6pm; a setpoint 0.5 C lower from 17:00 keeps the evening crowd longer, the rest of the day is a normal weekday

experiment.setup: four Fridays with -0.5 C from 17:00 vs four without
experiment.limitations: eight Fridays; one had a public holiday eve

r11.question: what settings suit this cafe on a public holiday?
r11.prediction: on a public holiday the lunch crowd arrives about an hour later than on a weekday; moving the lunch block to 13:00-15:00 may fit better, not yet settled

experiment.setup: three public holidays vs weekday average
experiment.success_criteria: peak at 13:00 or later on all three
experiment.limitations: three holidays; no settings change tested yet

r12.question: what settings work on a fair & warm day?
r12.prediction: on a fair and warm day the baseline settings hold; no adjustment tested has beaten them

experiment.setup: ten fair, warm days alternating baseline and -0.5 C
experiment.success_criteria: the adjusted days beat the baseline
